title: FetchFailure is imported from the ledger (OD-12, half 1 of 2)
body:
**Half one of two.** The code half of **OD-12**, split so neither half is red on a required check. Recorded as **ESC-25** and its correction row.

This pull request moves one import in `tests/test_ledger.py`. It takes `FetchFailure` from `ledger.py`, where the type has always been defined. Nothing else changes.

**Why the split.** `test-the-tests` reverts a pull request's implementation and requires the suite to go red. Retiring the re-export shim adds no behaviour — `transcripts.FetchFailure` still resolves at run time either way, and the only thing removed is mypy's explicit `X as X` re-export marking, a TYPE-level constraint pytest cannot observe. So the whole change kept together can never satisfy that check. The owner chose the split over a red merge. `test-the-tests` skips this pull request because it touches no file under `src/`, which is honest and is why the escape exists to record it.

**Half two** removes the alias from `src/find_best_mobo/transcripts.py` and follows once this lands. The order matters: after this, nothing reaches `FetchFailure` through `transcripts`, so removing the alias is inert. Reversed, `mypy` fails.

Both commits carry `Split-Of: od-12-fetchfailure-shim`. No check reads that trailer — it is the third candidate ESC-25's correction row asks for, done by hand so this split is visible in the history rather than surviving only in the ledger.

**Plan.** `docs/plans/corpus-and-checkpoint.md`, whose OD-12 paragraph ratifies `FetchFailure`, `HaltTriggered` and `Ledger` in `ledger.py`. That paragraph is what orders this change. The branch carries the slug so the `plan` check resolves it — #176 was `feat/retire-fetchfailure-shim`, which resolved nothing and failed `plan` for it.

**No blind tests, and none apply.** This adds no test and changes no behaviour. It edits one import line of an existing test module.

1255 passing, unchanged. `ruff check .` clean, `mypy src tests` clean.
